clue.text: Duty for this French military group

parts.note: a duty is a task you are given
taken as written
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A French unit is assigned to a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a military unit assembled for one specific operation.

clue.text: Function well enough when there's no more credit?

parts.note: to buy on tick is to buy on credit
something over is finished, no more

explanation.surface: How does a business run once its credit has run out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's' is a link; TICK is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over idles steadily, so the idiom means running at a modest level.

clue.text: Doris can hurt, being scornful

indicators.note: hurt letters are damaged and reshaped, signalling an anagram of the two words before

explanation.surface: Doris has a cutting tongue and can wound with her mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' rearranges the eight letters of DORIS CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking, a close synonym of scornful.

clue.text: Disc that's disaster, Penny points out

parts.note: a flop is a failure or disaster

indicators.note: compass points E, N and N are taken out of the word that precedes

parts.note: the word penny written in full

explanation.surface: Penny remarks that a record was a commercial failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points out' removes the compass points E, N, N from PENNY, leaving PY; 'Penny' looks like a name but is just the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy is an old flexible computer storage disc.

clue.text: Draw two fellows, real characters going around

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the fellows, signalling a container
the letters of the word real move about, signalling an anagram

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A sketch of two men who are genuine personalities doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching, but it is the noun for a prize lottery; F for fellow is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a lottery-style prize draw.

clue.text: Use drill

definitions.meaning: to ... a right or power is to use it

explanation.definitionFit: Exercise as a verb means employ, and as a noun a practice drill.

clue.text: Crowd round live group

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a set is a group

explanation.surface: People gather round a band playing live.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to surround and press upon, like a crowd closing in.

clue.text: Herb's independent about church

parts.note: basil is a herb; the 's is a link meaning has
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Herb, a free spirit, is around the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name, but it is the plant basil.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large church of a particular style or status.

clue.text: Cast lines

parts.note: read as what the performers in a play speak, written down for them

explanation.definitionFit: A play's text gives the actors their spoken parts.

clue.text: Sad jerk admits scrap

indicators.note: the twitch word lets the scrap in, a container signal

parts.note: a tic is a jerky involuntary movement
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A miserable lout lets a fight slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests an idiot and 'scrap' a fight, but they mean twitch and shred.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means deeply distressing, close to sad.

clue.text: Take away motor parked by aristo

parts.note: motor is British slang for a car
a toff is an upper-class person, an aristo

explanation.surface: A nobleman leaves his car parked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parked by' is a link joining the pieces; TOFF is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cart off is to remove or carry away.

clue.text: In favour of being generous and granting a pardon

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
giving means being generous

explanation.surface: Someone who backs charity and shows mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiving describes someone who pardons offences readily.

clue.text: Davy with Ken growing straggly pointy beard

indicators.note: untidy growth turns the two names into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two men grow untidy pointed beards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing straggly' rearranges DAVY and KEN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vandyke is a neat pointed beard named after the painter Van Dyck.

clue.text: I had ten before time in charge — that's foolish

parts.note: I'd is the shortening of I had
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0

explanation.surface: Drinking ten before being on duty would be a silly idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' and 'that's' are links; ten is written IO for the digits 1 0.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means extremely stupid, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Second thoughts about respect

parts.note: re means about or concerning
consideration means regard or respect

explanation.surface: Having doubts over whether to show esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Having second thoughts means thinking a decision over again.

clue.text: MP on lane, disguised by gaslight

indicators.note: something disguised changes its appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician in a street, his face concealed by a gas lamp's glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges MP ON LANE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon lamp is a glowing tube filled with gas, hence a gas light.

clue.text: One is not able to sleep through it

definitions.text: One is not able to sleep through it

parts.words: One is not able to sleep through it
parts.note: read as a condition of sleeplessness rather than something too noisy to ignore

explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is chronic inability to fall or stay asleep.

clue.text: Tell close friend

definitions.meaning: to hint at or make known

explanation.definitionFit: Intimate as a verb means hint or tell, and as a noun a confidant.

clue.text: Place on the other side of the Channel two diminutive boys

definitions.text: Place on the other side of the Channel

parts.note: Norm is short for Norman
Andy is short for Andrew

explanation.surface: Two small lads live just across the water in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminutive' means short forms of names, not small boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France facing England across the Channel.

clue.text: Eastern cape captured by Scottish poet is where in France?

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the French word inside, a container signal

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet
ou is French for where

explanation.surface: A headland in the East seized by Burns, a puzzle about its French location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a headland but is a cloak; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnous is a long hooded cloak worn by Arabs and Berbers.

clue.text: Counter blow

explanation.definitionFit: Buffet means a serving counter and also a knock or blow.

clue.text: Thunderous noise coming from bellyache — not good!

indicators.note: the letter for good is not present, so it is removed

parts.note: to bellyache is to grumble

explanation.surface: A loud stomach rumbling caused by a bad stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bellyache' suggests a stomach pain but means complain; 'coming from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumble is a deep rolling sound like thunder.

clue.text: The girl being tossed about in boat

indicators.note: things tossed about are scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl is thrown around in a boat on rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships.

clue.text: Glance towards part that's pointed

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, signalling a hidden run of letters

explanation.surface: Looking at a sharp-ended section.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a pointed surgical blade, also a pointed arch or window.

clue.text: One turn then another stopping short of the truth

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: the word ends early, losing its final letter

parts.note: a spell is another word for a turn or stint

explanation.surface: After a few turns, someone stops just before telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' cuts the last L from SPELL; 'then' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel means absolute truth, as in taking something as gospel.

clue.text: Many a film upset chap with wife and kids

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with a family is disturbed by many films.
explanation.definitionFit: A family man is a husband and father devoted to home life.

clue.text: Director on board?

parts.note: read as someone in command aboard a ship, not a company boardroom member

explanation.definitionFit: A captain commands a ship, directing those aboard.

clue.text: Fool wept tears about Romeo

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround the NATO letter, a container signal
tears as a verb means rips apart, so the word wept is rearranged

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A fool cried over his Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like crying but rips WEPT into TWEP, and 'about' puts that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a fool.

clue.text: Weapons in Welsh town, be gone!

indicators.note: the two letters spelt out are gone, removed from the town

parts.note: Abertillery is a town in south Wales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Guns in a Welsh town, told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; ABERTILLERY is a former mining town in Blaenau Gwent.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery means large guns and other heavy weapons.
